title: Find Minimum Time to Finish All Jobs II
summary: Given two 0-indexed integer arrays, jobs and workers, where jobs[i] represents the time needed to complete the i-th job, and workers[j] represents the amount of time the j-th worker can work each day, assign each job to exactly one worker such that each worker is assigned exactly one job.
statement: Given two 0-indexed integer arrays, jobs and workers, where jobs[i] represents the time needed to complete the i-th job, and workers[j] represents the amount of time the j-th worker can work each day, assign each job to exactly one worker such that each worker is assigned exactly one job. Determine the minimum number of days required to complete all the jobs after the assignments.
constraints: jobs and workers have equal length up to 100000; each positive worker capacity is work completed per day.
Assign exactly one job to each worker and one worker to each job.
Minimize the maximum ceiling(job_size/worker_capacity) across assignments.
hints: For a proposed day limit, a worker can handle every job no larger than days*capacity.
Sorting both sides pairs their ranks and avoids crossing assignments.
Pair sorted jobs with sorted workers and take the maximum ceiling ratio.
If two assignments cross, swapping them into sorted order cannot worsen their larger completion ratio; repeated exchanges yield the sorted optimum.
editorial: If two assignments cross, swapping them into sorted order cannot worsen their larger completion ratio; repeated exchanges yield the sorted optimum.

tests.explanation: Pairing jobs and workers in sorted order finishes every job within two days.
Sorted pairing yields completion times three, three, three, and three, so the answer is three days.
